description: Machine-readable registry of owner-scoped safety and liveness invariants. Contract records and Quest theory metadata cite these entries by id so coupling is checked structurally rather than as prose. Validate with `npm run model:invariants`.

invariants.statement: A node can never be published before its snapshot coverage is accepted; published is always a subset of covered.
A node with accepted snapshot coverage has already been reconciled by the owner; covered and pending never intersect.
Under weak fairness of the progress actions and bounded owner re-entry, every node eventually reaches published with a fresh quorum snapshot, so the active gate eventually goes green.

Only startup_active_gate_owner decides cluster ACTIVE; node lifecycle status, membership publication counts, cache coverage, and admin or harness projections are evidence or presentation and cannot independently authorize convergence.

Caller urgency, force intent, or successful-result reuse bypass cannot override an active failed-repair defer decision owned by authoritative_discovery_repair_owner; retry-after and single-flight pressure containment remain binding until the owner re-admits repair.
A reconciled-but-not-yet-published node may be deferred back to pending only a bounded number of times; unbounded deferred owner re-entry is the higher-level oscillation that prevents convergence.
Every state transition, lifecycle decision, data transformation, cache view, diagnostic grammar, and runtime resource has exactly one semantic owner.
Runtime logic consumes normalized state and does not reopen raw storage, transport, bootstrap, cache, or wire shapes.
An owner emits one canonical outcome before observers, caches, diagnostics, admin views, or harness reports project the result.
Reader-local caches, diagnostics, and reports do not repair or replace authoritative owner state on the hot path.
Degraded or cross-plane evidence can explain, defer, or block, but cannot upgrade readiness or admission.
Temporary bootstrap, join, recovery, and migration owners transfer responsibility to explicit steady-state owners before phase completion.
A stale observer projection cannot promote readiness, admission, or owner progress across handoff boundaries.
Every durable owner transition that requires follow-up work has an atomic, recoverable, or replayable wake before observers depend on it.
Every retry, rerun, handoff, or observer evidence combination emits exactly one owner-owned canonical action.
Repeated local retry with non-shrinking evidence cannot authorize another local retry.
Deferred follow-up work exits through a recoverable wake while retry budget remains available.
Startup readiness cannot become active before SQL and query transport serviceability are true for the canonical leader and the observed owner epoch is fresh.
Every deferred startup readiness handoff eventually reaches ready, blocked, or escalated under fair progress and recoverable wakes.
If missingPublishedCount > 0 and the local node is the publication owner, then a scheduled reconcile obligation is enabled.
A follower grants its vote to at most one candidate per term, so at most one leader can be elected per term (Raft §5.2 Election Safety).
invariants.formalPredicate: \A f, term: Cardinality({ c : VoteGranted(f, c, term) }) \leq 1

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-041 deterministic repro asserts grantedTo.length == 1 (a follower with a log grants at most one vote in a term) and exits 0

invariants.statement: A committed Raft log entry is identical cluster-wide at its index; a follower never stale-commits its own same-index/different-term entry on catch-up (Raft §5.3 Log Matching).
invariants.formalPredicate: \A i: committed(i) => \A n, m: log[n][i] = log[m][i]

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-040 deterministic repro asserts a follower does not stale-commit its own same-index entry on heal and exits 0

invariants.statement: A surplus-drain REPLACE whose declared source replica is already removed terminalizes (reaches SAFE) instead of re-dispatching a source-leader handoff to a replica that no longer exists (CL-038).

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-038 deterministic repro asserts a source-removed REPLACE reaches SAFE (does not loop re-dispatching a dead handoff) and exits 0

invariants.statement: The strict-mode active-node projection retains an already-published node that is transport-alive and within the heartbeat grace through a transient heartbeat-stall trough, while never promoting a non-baseline node on that grace and still trimming a published node that is genuinely stale (CL-001 variant C).
invariants.formalPredicate: \A n: PublishedBaseline(n) /\ TransportAlive(n) /\ WithinHeartbeatGrace(n) => Retained(n); \A m: ~PublishedBaseline(m) => ~AdmittedByGrace(m)

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-001 deterministic repro asserts the strict-mode projection retains the published transport-alive trough node, keeps the never-published node out, trims the genuinely stale node, and attributes retention-grace misses; exits 0

invariants.statement: The stage-3 membership-publication planning-snapshot merge (the residual readiness-build cost CL-033's projection memo does not cover) is memoized per publisher node under the same planning-source revision discipline, so per-routing-call rebuild storms cannot freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout during recovery (CL-034).
invariants.formalPredicate: \A n, window: SourceRevisionStable(n, window) => HeavyMergeBuilds(n, window) \leq 1

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-034 deterministic repro counts heavy buildMembershipPublicationPlanningSnapshot/buildPriorityRecoveryPlanningProjection builds per routing call and asserts the merge memo collapses the per-call rebuild storm; goes red if the memo stops engaging; exits 0

invariants.statement: The priority-recovery planning projection is memoized per publisher node (build once, reuse while the source revision and stale-grace window hold), so the post-restart recovery hot path cannot rebuild the heavy projection per call and freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout (CL-033).
invariants.formalPredicate: \A n, window: SourceRevisionStable(n, window) => HeavyProjectionBuilds(n, window) \leq 1

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-033 deterministic repro exercises resolveMemoizedPriorityRecoveryPlanningProjectionSync directly, counts heavy builds, and asserts build-once/reuse; goes red if the memo is silently disabled; exits 0

invariants.statement: A replica's committed learner-to-voter raft promotion is seeded into its own node's local SERVICES row at voter-ready activation, so the REPLACE remove-safety gate observes the promotion instead of deferring on a stale learner/null raft_role forever (CL-035).

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-035 deterministic repro asserts seedLocalReplicaVoterRaftRole writes the locally-decided voting role into the real SystemTableCache row, the remove-safety gate accepts the seeded role, and the activation path is wired; exits 0

invariants.statement: An empty raft log's last-log-term is 0 (Raft §5.4.1): the log adapters never masquerade an empty log as up-to-date, so a voter holding committed entries denies an empty-log candidate regardless of the candidate's election term (CL-042).

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the CL-042 deterministic repro asserts a voter holding a committed entry DENIES an empty-log higher-term candidate and exits 0

invariants.statement: A failed or unavailable authoritative read never concludes the positive premise of a safety gate: admission gates fail closed into a typed defer/deny (the conflict-lane deferred-visibility throw; the topology guard's replica_inventory_unusable denial; the surplus REMOVE commit fence; the ledger quorum-spread confirmation). A hold may fail OPEN on a read gap only where blocking on the gap would itself deadlock convergence, and each fail-open hold names its deadlock witness: the over-target count-keyed create-lane hold (G1; fail-closing it would strand the surplus drain it exists to release) and the routine-direction ledger self-move serialization (a disruptive IDLE_ONLY self-move still fails closed). Advisory probes fail open only where a fail-closed enforcer remains downstream (the provisioning ledger-interlock probe defers to operation creation as the enforcing seam).

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the verdict-matrix test drives every enumerated admission predicate with a failed authoritative read and asserts its documented verdict — fail-closed gates throw or deny, the two named fail-open holds admit with their deadlock witness, and each fail-open carries a red-on-revert witness; exits 0

invariants.statement: After semantic-input quiescence the final complete token is published; during continuous churn completed tokens advance monotonically, dirty owners receive bounded round-robin service, and stale evidence never promotes readiness.

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the production-composition churn regression proves final-token completion, stale-negative admission, owner-generation fencing, and fresh one-shot decision equivalence; exits 0

invariants.statement: Continuous readiness source churn starts at most one heavy planning build globally per macrotask turn and permits a timer or heartbeat sentinel between every pair of heavy items.

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the production-composition churn regression and owner-key queue scheduler test prove one heavy item per injected macrotask with timer progress and round-robin service; exit 0

invariants.statement: A readiness-internal authoritative owner read uses a structural purpose and completes through a local or minimal owner/transport route with full-readiness recursion depth zero.

liveEvidence.holdsWhen: the structural read-authority regression threads readiness_internal through CDC owner-RPC and production query routing and asserts recursion depth zero while ordinary reads retain readiness policy; exits 0
